title: Dependability Maturity Journey — Initiative Map and Sprint Plan
content:
Purpose:
This working doc lays out a cross-functional initiative to lift Redwood services from ad-hoc reliability work to a repeatable dependability maturity pathway. Focus: establish measurable service-level objectives, clear handoffs between teams, a compact set of tooling integrations, and a six-month cadence of experiments that demonstrably reduce error-budget volatility and incident toil.

Background & motivation:
- Many product teams have informal expectations about reliability, but observability and response processes vary by service.
- Goal is to converge on a minimal, pragmatic set of commitments (service-level objectives), automate signal collection, and create a dependable process for rollouts and fallbacks.
- This doc is intentionally operational and lightweight: decision points, sprintable milestones, and owner-level actions.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: core-hosted inference routes, internal model-routing control plane, and dedup/caching layers that affect tail latency and token cost.
- Out-of-scope: billing pipeline, marketing-facing telemetry dashboards, and experimental research model training. Those will be handled by respective teams but surfaced for dependencies.

Objectives (measurable):
1) Define and publish service-level objectives (SLOs) for 6 pilot services within 8 weeks. Acceptance: SLO docs + SLIs instrumented + alert rules in Alertmanager.
2) Reduce P95 tail latency variance by 20% for pilot services across a representative workload in 12 weeks.
3) Implement automated fallback routing (model variant downgrade) for at least 2 high-priority routes with documented rollback playbooks.
4) Create an incident-to-OKR feedback loop: every major incident updates a test or rollout checklist within two sprints.

Stakeholders & responsibilities (RACI-lite):
- ENG-SRE (Maya Chen, lead): overall program coach, instrumentation standards, alerting templates, runbook templates.
- Serving Runtime (Ethan Morales): code changes to expose SLIs (latency histograms, headroom metrics) and client-side retry semantics.
- Platform Engineering (Priya Desai): routing policy implementation, canary configuration knobs, and traffic shaping support.
- Product / Hosted API (Lena Hoffman): prioritization for pilot routes, acceptance criteria, and customer-facing messaging.
- Solutions Engineering (Carlos Ruiz): validates rollback behavior against customer scenarios; coordinates with customers on test windows.

Dependability Maturity Levels (practical definitions):
- M1: Baseline visibility — basic metrics (QPS, error rate, latency) exist but are scattered; incident response ad-hoc.
  Acceptance: per-service metrics using shared naming conventions; incident timeline template.
- M2: Agreed objectives — SLIs and SLOs defined and enforced via alerts; basic runbooks for top 3 failure modes.
  Acceptance: SLO docs in Confluence + Alertmanager rules + runbook for primary incident path.
- M3: Automated mitigation — fallback policies, automated retries, and partial-rollout awareness; integration with cadence for rollouts.
  Acceptance: automated downgrade route + rehearsed rollback in staging; runbook verified via simulated failure.
- M4: Proactive capacity & regression controls — load prediction, cost-aware batching optimizations applied, and automated canary gating.
  Acceptance: Canary gates in CI that fail on SLO regressions; capacity forecast connected to autoscaler policies.

Six-week sprint plan (high level, split into 2-week sprints):
- Sprint 0 (week -1 to 0): kickoff, finalize pilot services, baseline telemetry audit. Outcomes: audit doc, list of missing metrics. Tickets: REL-2050 (telemetry audit).
- Sprint 1 (weeks 1–2): Implement shared SLI definitions and metrics naming. Create SLO templates in Confluence. Outcomes: SLO template, instrumented latency & error SLIs for pilot service A+B. Tickets: REL-2051, PR infra#842.
- Sprint 2 (weeks 3–4): Alert rules, runbook drafts, and incident response tabletop for pilot A. Outcomes: Alertmanager rules, runbook markdown, tabletop notes. Tickets: REL-2055.
- Sprint 3 (weeks 5–6): Implement fallback routing for pilot A, canary gating experiment for pilot B. Outcomes: fallback policy live in staging, canary gating added to pipeline. Tickets: REL-2062, PLAT-498.
- Sprint 4 (weeks 7–8): Measure post-change P95 variance and run a simulated failure to verify automation. Outcomes: experiment results, updated runbooks. Tickets: REL-2070.
- Sprint 5+ (weeks 9–24): Scale to remaining pilots, iterate on tooling, tighten metrics and SLA docs. Outcomes: all pilots at least M2, two at M3.

Cross-functional rituals & communications:
- Weekly 30m sync on Tuesdays (ENG-SRE + Serving Runtime + Platform); agenda: blockers, metrics snapshot, next actions.
- Biweekly stakeholder demo (30–45m) showing canary results and incident learnings.
- Incident postmortem + SLO regression review added to product retro agenda within two sprints.
- Slack channel: #dependability-journey (pin: runbook template, SLO template, key tickets).

Metrics & measurement plan (what we'll collect):
- SLIs: success_rate (5xx + user-visible errors), p95_latency_ms, request_headroom (capacity headroom fraction), queue_wait_time_ms, token_generation_error_rate.
- Derived metrics: error_budget_burn_rate (rolling 30d), SLO_compliance (binary per-day), alert_fatigue_index (#alerts / oncall-hours).
- Dashboards: per-route SLI panel, burn-rate heatmap, canary-gate pass/fail history.

Tooling & integration checklist:
- Prometheus/Tempo: ensure histograms for latencies and exemplars for trace linking.
- Alertmanager: template alerts derived from error_budget_burn_rate and p95 regressions. Use shared labels: service, route, environment.
- Console: add per-route SLO card and quick links to runbook and rollback action.
- CI: canary gate step that evaluates SLOs against baseline (script in infra repo).

Risk register (top items) + mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry gaps in legacy services. Mitigation: fallbacks to synthetic probes and synthetic canaries; backlog tickets prioritized.
- Risk: rollout complexity causes customer-facing regressions. Mitigation: staged rollout + customer-only canary flag; Solutions Eng validates.
- Risk: noisy alerts lead to ignoring burn signals. Mitigation: threshold tuning, suppress during planned work windows, and alert fatigue tracking.

Communication plan (customer & internal):
- Internal: publish weekly digest summarizing change windows, canary outcomes, and any service-level changes.
- Customer-facing: coordinated release notes for any change that alters SLOs or introduces fallbacks; product to approve.

Action log (short, sprint-owners, immediate next steps):
- Maya: finalize SLO template and publish to Confluence (REL-2051).
- Ethan: add latency histogram + headroom metric to pilot A (PR: infra#842).
- Priya: wire up canary gate script into CI (PLAT-498).
- Lena: notify customers for pilot A test window, prepare messaging.
- Carlos: schedule customer validation sessions and coordinate test scenarios.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Do we treat cached responses as separate SLOs? (pros/cons listed in notes below).
- What is an acceptable alert burn rate for infra teams vs product teams? Proposal: infra teams tolerate lower alert frequency but expect tight SLO ownership.
- Consider a lightweight ‘SLO health’ badge in console — scoped for later.

Appendix: quick checklists
- SLO checklist for a service: owner assigned, SLIs instrumented, Alertmanager rule, runbook skeleton, canary gating in CI, customer comms draft.
- Incident postmortem checklist: timeline, impact, root cause, SLO impact table, action with owner/ticket and due date.

Todo (short term):
- Push SLO template to Confluence (target: this week).
- Kick off telemetry audit (REL-2050).
- Book Tuesday weekly slot and create calendar invite (Maya).

This is intentionally a working document — expect edits. Tagging contributors: @ethan, @priya, @lena, @carlos.

Notes (end):
- If any team wants to opt a pilot out, request must include a mitigation plan and a ticket.
- After pilots reach M2, we’ll run a cross-team retro to codify the standard operating package for onboarding new services.
